lines.speaker: RODERIGO
lines.text: Iago—

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: What sayst thou, noble heart?

lines.speaker: RODERIGO
lines.text: What will I do, thinkest thou?

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: If thou dost, I shall never love thee after. Why, thou silly gentleman!

lines.speaker: RODERIGO
lines.text: It is silliness to live, when to live is torment; and then have we a

lines.speaker: RODERIGO
lines.text: prescription to die when death is our physician.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: O villainous! I have looked upon the world for four times seven years,

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: and since I could distinguish betwixt a benefit and an injury, I never

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: found man that knew how to love himself. Ere I would say I would drown

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: myself for the love of a guinea-hen, I would change my humanity with a

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: baboon.

lines.speaker: RODERIGO
lines.text: What should I do? I confess it is my shame to be so fond, but it is not

lines.speaker: RODERIGO
lines.text: in my virtue to amend it.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Virtue! a fig! ’Tis in ourselves that we are thus or thus. Our bodies

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: are gardens, to the which our wills are gardeners. So that if we will

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: plant nettles or sow lettuce, set hyssop and weed up thyme, supply it

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: with one gender of herbs or distract it with many, either to have it

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: sterile with idleness or manured with industry, why, the power and

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: corrigible authority of this lies in our wills. If the balance of our

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: lives had not one scale of reason to poise another of sensuality, the

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: blood and baseness of our natures would conduct us to most preposterous

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: conclusions. But we have reason to cool our raging motions, our carnal

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: stings, our unbitted lusts; whereof I take this, that you call love, to

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: be a sect, or scion.

lines.speaker: RODERIGO
lines.text: It cannot be.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: It is merely a lust of the blood and a permission of the will. Come, be

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: a man. Drown thyself? Drown cats and blind puppies. I have professed me

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: thy friend, and I confess me knit to thy deserving with cables of

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: perdurable toughness; I could never better stead thee than now. Put

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: money in thy purse; follow thou the wars; defeat thy favour with an

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: usurped beard; I say, put money in thy purse. It cannot be that

lines.speaker: IAGO

lines.text: purse,—nor he his to her. It was a violent commencement, and thou shalt

lines.speaker: IAGO

lines.speaker: IAGO

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: thou canst. If sanctimony and a frail vow betwixt an erring barbarian

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: tribe of hell, thou shalt enjoy her; therefore make money. A pox of

lines.speaker: IAGO

lines.speaker: IAGO

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: sport. There are many events in the womb of time which will be

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: delivered. Traverse, go, provide thy money. We will have more of this

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: tomorrow. Adieu.

lines.speaker: RODERIGO

lines.speaker: MONTANO
lines.text: Nay, good lieutenant;

lines.speaker: MONTANO
lines.text: I pray you, sir, hold your hand.

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: Let me go, sir,

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: Or I’ll knock you o’er the mazard.

lines.speaker: MONTANO
lines.text: Come, come, you’re drunk.

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: Drunk?
[_They fight._]
[_Aside to Roderigo._]

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Away, I say! Go out and cry a mutiny.
[_Exit Roderigo._]

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Nay, good lieutenant, God’s will, gentlemen.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Help, ho!—Lieutenant,—sir,—Montano,—sir:—

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Help, masters! Here’s a goodly watch indeed!
[_A bell rings._]

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Who’s that which rings the bell?—Diablo, ho!

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: The town will rise. God’s will, lieutenant, hold,

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: You will be sham’d forever.
Enter Othello and Attendants.

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: What is the matter here?

lines.speaker: MONTANO
lines.text: Zounds, I bleed still, I am hurt to the death.

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: Hold, for your lives!

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Hold, ho! lieutenant,—sir,—Montano,—gentlemen,—

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Have you forgot all place of sense and duty?

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Hold! The general speaks to you; hold, hold, for shame!

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: Why, how now, ho! From whence ariseth this?

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: Are we turn’d Turks, and to ourselves do that

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: Which heaven hath forbid the Ottomites?

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: For Christian shame, put by this barbarous brawl:

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: He that stirs next to carve for his own rage

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: Holds his soul light; he dies upon his motion.

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: Silence that dreadful bell, it frights the isle

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: From her propriety. What is the matter, masters?

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: Honest Iago, that looks dead with grieving,

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: Speak, who began this? On thy love, I charge thee.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: I do not know. Friends all but now, even now,

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: In quarter, and in terms like bride and groom

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Devesting them for bed; and then, but now,

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: As if some planet had unwitted men,

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Swords out, and tilting one at other’s breast,

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: In opposition bloody. I cannot speak

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Any beginning to this peevish odds;

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: And would in action glorious I had lost

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Those legs that brought me to a part of it!

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: How comes it, Michael, you are thus forgot?

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: I pray you, pardon me; I cannot speak.

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: Worthy Montano, you were wont be civil.

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: The gravity and stillness of your youth

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: The world hath noted, and your name is great

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: In mouths of wisest censure: what’s the matter,

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: That you unlace your reputation thus,

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: And spend your rich opinion for the name

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: Of a night-brawler? Give me answer to it.

lines.speaker: MONTANO
lines.text: Worthy Othello, I am hurt to danger.

lines.speaker: MONTANO
lines.text: Your officer, Iago, can inform you,

lines.speaker: MONTANO
lines.text: While I spare speech, which something now offends me,

lines.speaker: MONTANO
lines.text: Of all that I do know; nor know I aught

lines.speaker: MONTANO
lines.text: By me that’s said or done amiss this night,

lines.speaker: MONTANO
lines.text: Unless self-charity be sometimes a vice,

lines.speaker: MONTANO
lines.text: And to defend ourselves it be a sin

lines.speaker: MONTANO
lines.text: When violence assails us.

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: Now, by heaven,

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: My blood begins my safer guides to rule,

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: And passion, having my best judgement collied,

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: Assays to lead the way. Zounds, if I stir,

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: Or do but lift this arm, the best of you

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: Shall sink in my rebuke. Give me to know

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: How this foul rout began, who set it on,

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: And he that is approv’d in this offence,

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: Though he had twinn’d with me, both at a birth,

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: Shall lose me. What! in a town of war,

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: Yet wild, the people’s hearts brimful of fear,

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: To manage private and domestic quarrel,

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: In night, and on the court and guard of safety?

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: ’Tis monstrous. Iago, who began’t?

lines.speaker: MONTANO
lines.text: If partially affin’d, or leagu’d in office,

lines.speaker: MONTANO
lines.text: Thou dost deliver more or less than truth,

lines.speaker: MONTANO
lines.text: Thou art no soldier.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Touch me not so near.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: I had rather have this tongue cut from my mouth

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Than it should do offence to Michael Cassio.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Yet I persuade myself, to speak the truth

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Shall nothing wrong him. Thus it is, general:

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Montano and myself being in speech,

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: There comes a fellow crying out for help,

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: And Cassio following him with determin’d sword,

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: To execute upon him. Sir, this gentleman

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Steps in to Cassio and entreats his pause.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Myself the crying fellow did pursue,

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Lest by his clamour (as it so fell out)

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: The town might fall in fright: he, swift of foot,

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Outran my purpose: and I return’d the rather

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: For that I heard the clink and fall of swords,

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: And Cassio high in oath, which till tonight

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: I ne’er might say before. When I came back,

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: (For this was brief) I found them close together,

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: At blow and thrust, even as again they were

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: When you yourself did part them.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: More of this matter cannot I report.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: But men are men; the best sometimes forget;

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Though Cassio did some little wrong to him,

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: As men in rage strike those that wish them best,

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Yet surely Cassio, I believe, receiv’d

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: From him that fled some strange indignity,

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Which patience could not pass.

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: I know, Iago,

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: Thy honesty and love doth mince this matter,

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: Making it light to Cassio. Cassio, I love thee,

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: But never more be officer of mine.
Enter Desdemona, attended.

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: Look, if my gentle love be not rais’d up!

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: I’ll make thee an example.

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: What’s the matter?

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: All’s well now, sweeting; come away to bed.

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: Sir, for your hurts, myself will be your surgeon.

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: Lead him off.
[_Montano is led off._]

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: Iago, look with care about the town,

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: And silence those whom this vile brawl distracted.

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: Come, Desdemona: ’tis the soldiers’ life

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: To have their balmy slumbers wak’d with strife.
[_Exeunt all but Iago and Cassio._]

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: What, are you hurt, lieutenant?

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: Ay, past all surgery.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Marry, Heaven forbid!

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: Reputation, reputation, reputation! O, I have lost my reputation! I

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: have lost the immortal part of myself, and what remains is bestial. My

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: reputation, Iago, my reputation!

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: As I am an honest man, I thought you had received some bodily wound;

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: there is more sense in that than in reputation. Reputation is an idle

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: and most false imposition, oft got without merit and lost without

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: deserving. You have lost no reputation at all, unless you repute

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: yourself such a loser. What, man, there are ways to recover the general

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: again: you are but now cast in his mood, a punishment more in policy

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: than in malice, even so as one would beat his offenceless dog to

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: affright an imperious lion: sue to him again, and he’s yours.

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: I will rather sue to be despised than to deceive so good a commander

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: with so slight, so drunken, and so indiscreet an officer. Drunk? and

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: speak parrot? and squabble? swagger? swear? and discourse fustian with

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: one’s own shadow? O thou invisible spirit of wine, if thou hast no name

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: to be known by, let us call thee devil!

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: What was he that you followed with your sword? What had he done to you?

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: I know not.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Is’t possible?

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: I remember a mass of things, but nothing distinctly; a quarrel, but

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: nothing wherefore. O God, that men should put an enemy in their mouths

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: to steal away their brains! That we should with joy, pleasance, revel,

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: and applause, transform ourselves into beasts!

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Why, but you are now well enough: how came you thus recovered?

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: It hath pleased the devil drunkenness to give place to the devil wrath.

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: One unperfectness shows me another, to make me frankly despise myself.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Come, you are too severe a moraler. As the time, the place, and the

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: condition of this country stands, I could heartily wish this had not

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: befallen; but since it is as it is, mend it for your own good.

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: I will ask him for my place again; he shall tell me I am a drunkard!

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: Had I as many mouths as Hydra, such an answer would stop them all. To

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: be now a sensible man, by and by a fool, and presently a beast! O

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: strange! Every inordinate cup is unbless’d, and the ingredient is a

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: devil.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Come, come, good wine is a good familiar creature, if it be well used.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Exclaim no more against it. And, good lieutenant, I think you think I

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: love you.

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: I have well approved it, sir.—I drunk!

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: You, or any man living, may be drunk at a time, man. I’ll tell you what

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: you shall do. Our general’s wife is now the general; I may say so in

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: this respect, for that he hath devoted and given up himself to the

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: contemplation, mark, and denotement of her parts and graces. Confess

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: yourself freely to her. Importune her help to put you in your place

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: again. She is of so free, so kind, so apt, so blessed a disposition,

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: she holds it a vice in her goodness not to do more than she is

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: requested. This broken joint between you and her husband entreat her to

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: splinter, and, my fortunes against any lay worth naming, this crack of

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: your love shall grow stronger than it was before.

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: You advise me well.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: I protest, in the sincerity of love and honest kindness.

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: I think it freely; and betimes in the morning I will beseech the

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: virtuous Desdemona to undertake for me; I am desperate of my fortunes

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: if they check me here.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: You are in the right. Good night, lieutenant, I must to the watch.

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: Good night, honest Iago.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: And what’s he then, that says I play the villain?

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: When this advice is free I give and honest,

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Probal to thinking, and indeed the course

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: To win the Moor again? For ’tis most easy

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: The inclining Desdemona to subdue

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: In any honest suit. She’s fram’d as fruitful

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: As the free elements. And then for her

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: To win the Moor, were’t to renounce his baptism,

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: All seals and symbols of redeemed sin,

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: His soul is so enfetter’d to her love

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: That she may make, unmake, do what she list,

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Even as her appetite shall play the god

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: With his weak function. How am I then, a villain

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: To counsel Cassio to this parallel course,

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Directly to his good? Divinity of hell!

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: When devils will the blackest sins put on,

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: They do suggest at first with heavenly shows,

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: As I do now: for whiles this honest fool

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Plies Desdemona to repair his fortune,

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: And she for him pleads strongly to the Moor,

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: I’ll pour this pestilence into his ear,

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: That she repeals him for her body’s lust;

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: And by how much she strives to do him good,

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: She shall undo her credit with the Moor.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: So will I turn her virtue into pitch,

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: And out of her own goodness make the net

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: That shall enmesh them all.
Enter Roderigo.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: How now, Roderigo?

lines.speaker: RODERIGO
lines.text: I do follow here in the chase, not like a hound that hunts, but one

lines.speaker: RODERIGO
lines.text: that fills up the cry. My money is almost spent, I have been tonight

lines.speaker: RODERIGO
lines.text: exceedingly well cudgelled; and I think the issue will be, I shall have

lines.speaker: RODERIGO
lines.text: so much experience for my pains, and so, with no money at all and a

lines.speaker: RODERIGO
lines.text: little more wit, return again to Venice.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: How poor are they that have not patience!

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: What wound did ever heal but by degrees?

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Thou know’st we work by wit, and not by witchcraft,

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: And wit depends on dilatory time.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Does’t not go well? Cassio hath beaten thee,

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: And thou, by that small hurt, hast cashier’d Cassio;

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Though other things grow fair against the sun,

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Yet fruits that blossom first will first be ripe.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Content thyself awhile. By the mass, ’tis morning;

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Pleasure and action make the hours seem short.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Retire thee; go where thou art billeted.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Away, I say, thou shalt know more hereafter.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Nay, get thee gone.
[_Exit Roderigo._]

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Two things are to be done,

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: My wife must move for Cassio to her mistress.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: I’ll set her on;

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Myself the while to draw the Moor apart,

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: And bring him jump when he may Cassio find

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Soliciting his wife. Ay, that’s the way.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Dull not device by coldness and delay.
[_Exit._]
Enter Cassio and some Musicians.

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: Masters, play here, I will content your pains,

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: Something that’s brief; and bid “Good morrow, general.”
[_Music._]
Enter Clown.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Why, masters, have your instruments been in Naples, that they speak i’

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: the nose thus?

lines.speaker: FIRST MUSICIAN
lines.text: How, sir, how?

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Are these, I pray you, wind instruments?

lines.speaker: FIRST MUSICIAN
lines.text: Ay, marry, are they, sir.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: O, thereby hangs a tail.

lines.speaker: FIRST MUSICIAN
lines.text: Whereby hangs a tale, sir?

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Marry, sir, by many a wind instrument that I know. But, masters, here’s

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: money for you: and the general so likes your music, that he desires

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: you, for love’s sake, to make no more noise with it.

lines.speaker: FIRST MUSICIAN
lines.text: Well, sir, we will not.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: If you have any music that may not be heard, to’t again. But, as they

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: say, to hear music the general does not greatly care.

lines.speaker: FIRST MUSICIAN
lines.text: We have none such, sir.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Then put up your pipes in your bag, for I’ll away. Go, vanish into air,

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: away!
[_Exeunt Musicians._]

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: Dost thou hear, mine honest friend?

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: No, I hear not your honest friend. I hear you.

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: Prithee, keep up thy quillets. There’s a poor piece of gold for thee:

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: if the gentlewoman that attends the general’s wife be stirring, tell

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: her there’s one Cassio entreats her a little favour of speech. Wilt

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: thou do this?

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: She is stirring, sir; if she will stir hither, I shall seem to notify

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: unto her.

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: Do, good my friend.
[_Exit Clown._]
Enter Iago.

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: In happy time, Iago.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: You have not been a-bed, then?

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: Why, no. The day had broke

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: Before we parted. I have made bold, Iago,

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: To send in to your wife. My suit to her

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: Is, that she will to virtuous Desdemona

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: Procure me some access.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: I’ll send her to you presently,

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: And I’ll devise a mean to draw the Moor

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Out of the way, that your converse and business

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: May be more free.

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: I humbly thank you for’t.
[_Exit Iago._]

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: I never knew

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: A Florentine more kind and honest.
Enter Emilia.

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: Good morrow, good lieutenant; I am sorry

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: For your displeasure, but all will sure be well.

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: The general and his wife are talking of it,

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: And she speaks for you stoutly: the Moor replies

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: That he you hurt is of great fame in Cyprus

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: And great affinity, and that in wholesome wisdom

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: He might not but refuse you; but he protests he loves you

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: And needs no other suitor but his likings

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: To take the safest occasion by the front

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: To bring you in again.

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: Yet, I beseech you,

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: If you think fit, or that it may be done,

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: Give me advantage of some brief discourse

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: With Desdemona alone.

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: Pray you, come in.

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: I will bestow you where you shall have time

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: To speak your bosom freely.

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: I am much bound to you.
[_Exeunt._]

lines.text: These letters give, Iago, to the pilot,

lines.text: And by him do my duties to the senate.

lines.speaker: OTHELLO

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: Repair there to me.

lines.text: handkerchief you gave me even now? I was a fine fool to take it. I must

lines.text: take out the work? A likely piece of work, that you should find it in

[_Coming forward._]

lines.text: Nay, you must forget that.

lines.text: Nay, that’s certain. But yet the pity of it, Iago! O Iago, the pity of

lines.text: I will chop her into messes. Cuckold me!

lines.text: That I may save my speech: do but go after,

lines.text: What place? what time? what form? what likelihood?

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: The Moor’s abused by some most villainous knave,

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: Some base notorious knave, some scurvy fellow.

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: O heaven, that such companions thou’dst unfold,

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: And put in every honest hand a whip

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: To lash the rascals naked through the world

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: Even from the east to the west!

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Speak within door.

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: O, fie upon them! Some such squire he was

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: That turn’d your wit the seamy side without,

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: And made you to suspect me with the Moor.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: You are a fool. Go to.

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: Alas, Iago,

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: What shall I do to win my lord again?

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: Good friend, go to him. For by this light of heaven,

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: I know not how I lost him. Here I kneel.

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: If e’er my will did trespass ’gainst his love,

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: Either in discourse of thought or actual deed,

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: Or that mine eyes, mine ears, or any sense,

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: Delighted them in any other form,

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: Or that I do not yet, and ever did,

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: And ever will, (though he do shake me off

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: To beggarly divorcement) love him dearly,

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: Comfort forswear me! Unkindness may do much;

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: And his unkindness may defeat my life,

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: But never taint my love. I cannot say “whore,”

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: It does abhor me now I speak the word;

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: To do the act that might the addition earn

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: Not the world’s mass of vanity could make me.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: I pray you, be content. ’Tis but his humour.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: The business of the state does him offence,

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: And he does chide with you.

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: If ’twere no other,—

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: ’Tis but so, I warrant.
[_Trumpets within._]

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Hark, how these instruments summon to supper.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: The messengers of Venice stay the meat.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Go in, and weep not. All things shall be well.
[_Exeunt Desdemona and Emilia._]
Enter Roderigo.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: How now, Roderigo?

lines.speaker: RODERIGO
lines.text: I do not find that thou dealest justly with me.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: What in the contrary?

lines.speaker: RODERIGO
lines.text: Every day thou daffest me with some device, Iago, and rather, as it

lines.speaker: RODERIGO
lines.text: seems to me now, keepest from me all conveniency than suppliest me with

lines.speaker: RODERIGO
lines.text: the least advantage of hope. I will indeed no longer endure it. Nor am

lines.speaker: RODERIGO
lines.text: I yet persuaded to put up in peace what already I have foolishly

lines.speaker: RODERIGO
lines.text: suffered.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Will you hear me, Roderigo?

lines.speaker: RODERIGO
lines.text: Faith, I have heard too much, for your words and performances are no

lines.speaker: RODERIGO
lines.text: kin together.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: You charge me most unjustly.

lines.speaker: RODERIGO
lines.text: With naught but truth. I have wasted myself out of my means. The jewels

lines.speaker: RODERIGO
lines.text: you have had from me to deliver to Desdemona would half have corrupted

lines.speaker: RODERIGO
lines.text: a votarist: you have told me she hath received them, and returned me

lines.speaker: RODERIGO
lines.text: expectations and comforts of sudden respect and acquaintance, but I

lines.speaker: RODERIGO
lines.text: find none.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Well, go to, very well.

lines.speaker: RODERIGO
lines.text: Very well, go to, I cannot go to, man, nor ’tis not very well. Nay, I

lines.speaker: RODERIGO
lines.text: say ’tis very scurvy, and begin to find myself fopped in it.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Very well.

lines.speaker: RODERIGO
lines.text: I tell you ’tis not very well. I will make myself known to Desdemona.

lines.speaker: RODERIGO
lines.text: If she will return me my jewels, I will give over my suit and repent my

lines.speaker: RODERIGO
lines.text: unlawful solicitation. If not, assure yourself I will seek satisfaction

lines.speaker: RODERIGO
lines.text: of you.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: You have said now.

lines.speaker: RODERIGO
lines.text: Ay, and said nothing but what I protest intendment of doing.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Why, now I see there’s mettle in thee, and even from this instant do

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: build on thee a better opinion than ever before. Give me thy hand,

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Roderigo. Thou hast taken against me a most just exception, but yet I

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: protest, I have dealt most directly in thy affair.

lines.speaker: RODERIGO
lines.text: It hath not appeared.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: I grant indeed it hath not appeared, and your suspicion is not without

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: wit and judgement. But, Roderigo, if thou hast that in thee indeed,

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: which I have greater reason to believe now than ever,—I mean purpose,

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: courage, and valour,—this night show it. If thou the next night

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: following enjoy not Desdemona, take me from this world with treachery

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: and devise engines for my life.

lines.speaker: RODERIGO
lines.text: Well, what is it? Is it within reason and compass?

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Sir, there is especial commission come from Venice to depute Cassio in

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Othello’s place.

lines.speaker: RODERIGO
lines.text: Is that true? Why then Othello and Desdemona return again to Venice.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: O, no; he goes into Mauritania, and takes away with him the fair

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Desdemona, unless his abode be lingered here by some accident: wherein

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: none can be so determinate as the removing of Cassio.

lines.speaker: RODERIGO
lines.text: How do you mean “removing” of him?

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Why, by making him uncapable of Othello’s place: knocking out his

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: brains.

lines.speaker: RODERIGO
lines.text: And that you would have me to do?

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Ay, if you dare do yourself a profit and a right. He sups tonight with

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: a harlotry, and thither will I go to him. He knows not yet of his

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: honourable fortune. If you will watch his going thence, which I will

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: fashion to fall out between twelve and one, you may take him at your

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: pleasure: I will be near to second your attempt, and he shall fall

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: between us. Come, stand not amazed at it, but go along with me. I will

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: show you such a necessity in his death that you shall think yourself

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: bound to put it on him. It is now high supper-time, and the night grows

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: to waste. About it.

lines.speaker: RODERIGO
lines.text: I will hear further reason for this.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: And you shall be satisfied.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: Cyprus. Another Room in the Castle.

lines.text: Enter Othello, Lodovico, Desdemona, Emilia and Attendants.

lines.speaker: LODOVICO
lines.text: I do beseech you, sir, trouble yourself no further.

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: O, pardon me; ’twill do me good to walk.

lines.speaker: LODOVICO
lines.text: Madam, good night. I humbly thank your ladyship.

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: Your honour is most welcome.

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: Will you walk, sir?—

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: O, Desdemona,—

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: My lord?

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: Get you to bed on th’ instant, I will be return’d forthwith. Dismiss

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: your attendant there. Look ’t be done.

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: I will, my lord.
[_Exeunt Othello, Lodovico and Attendants._]

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: How goes it now? He looks gentler than he did.

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: He says he will return incontinent,

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: He hath commanded me to go to bed,

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: And bade me to dismiss you.

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: Dismiss me?

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: It was his bidding. Therefore, good Emilia,

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: Give me my nightly wearing, and adieu.

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: We must not now displease him.

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: I would you had never seen him!

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: So would not I. My love doth so approve him,

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: That even his stubbornness, his checks, his frowns,—

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: Prithee, unpin me,—have grace and favour in them.

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: I have laid those sheets you bade me on the bed.

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: All’s one. Good faith, how foolish are our minds!

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: If I do die before thee, prithee, shroud me

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: In one of those same sheets.

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: Come, come, you talk.

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: My mother had a maid call’d Barbary,

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: She was in love, and he she lov’d prov’d mad

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: And did forsake her. She had a song of “willow”,

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: An old thing ’twas, but it express’d her fortune,

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: And she died singing it. That song tonight

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: Will not go from my mind. I have much to do

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: But to go hang my head all at one side

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: And sing it like poor Barbary. Prithee dispatch.

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: Shall I go fetch your night-gown?

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: No, unpin me here.

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: This Lodovico is a proper man.

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: A very handsome man.

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: He speaks well.

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: I know a lady in Venice would have walked barefoot to Palestine for a

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: touch of his nether lip.
[_Singing._]

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: _The poor soul sat sighing by a sycamore tree,

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: Sing all a green willow.

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: Her hand on her bosom, her head on her knee,

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: Sing willow, willow, willow.

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: The fresh streams ran by her, and murmur’d her moans,

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: Sing willow, willow, willow;

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: Her salt tears fell from her, and soften’d the stones;—_

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: Lay by these:—
[_Sings._]

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: _Sing willow, willow, willow._

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: Prithee hie thee. He’ll come anon.
[_Sings._]

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: _Sing all a green willow must be my garland.

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: Let nobody blame him, his scorn I approve,—_

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: Nay, that’s not next. Hark! who is’t that knocks?

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: It’s the wind.
[_Sings._]

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: _I call’d my love false love; but what said he then?

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: Sing willow, willow, willow:

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: If I court mo women, you’ll couch with mo men._

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: So get thee gone; good night. Mine eyes do itch;

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: Doth that bode weeping?

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: ’Tis neither here nor there.

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: I have heard it said so. O, these men, these men!

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: Dost thou in conscience think,—tell me, Emilia,—

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: That there be women do abuse their husbands

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: In such gross kind?

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: There be some such, no question.

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: Wouldst thou do such a deed for all the world?

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: Why, would not you?

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: No, by this heavenly light!

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: Nor I neither by this heavenly light,

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: I might do’t as well i’ the dark.

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: Wouldst thou do such a deed for all the world?

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: The world’s a huge thing. It is a great price

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: For a small vice.

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: In troth, I think thou wouldst not.

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: In troth, I think I should, and undo’t when I had done. Marry, I would

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: not do such a thing for a joint-ring, nor for measures of lawn, nor for

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: gowns, petticoats, nor caps, nor any petty exhibition; but, for the

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: whole world—why, who would not make her husband a cuckold to make him a

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: monarch? I should venture purgatory for ’t.

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: Beshrew me, if I would do such a wrong for the whole world.

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: Why, the wrong is but a wrong i’ the world; and having the world for

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: your labour, ’tis a wrong in your own world, and you might quickly make

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: it right.

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: I do not think there is any such woman.

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: Yes, a dozen; and as many to the vantage as would store the world they

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: played for.

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: But I do think it is their husbands’ faults

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: If wives do fall: say that they slack their duties,

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: And pour our treasures into foreign laps;

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: Or else break out in peevish jealousies,

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: Throwing restraint upon us. Or say they strike us,

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: Or scant our former having in despite.

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: Why, we have galls; and though we have some grace,

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: Yet have we some revenge. Let husbands know

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: Their wives have sense like them: they see, and smell

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: And have their palates both for sweet and sour,

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: As husbands have. What is it that they do

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: When they change us for others? Is it sport?

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: I think it is. And doth affection breed it?

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: I think it doth. Is’t frailty that thus errs?

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: It is so too. And have not we affections,

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: Desires for sport, and frailty, as men have?

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: Then let them use us well: else let them know,

lines.speaker: EMILIA
lines.text: The ills we do, their ills instruct us so.

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: Good night, good night. Heaven me such usage send,

lines.speaker: DESDEMONA
lines.text: Not to pick bad from bad, but by bad mend!
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Iago and Roderigo.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Here, stand behind this bulk. Straight will he come.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Wear thy good rapier bare, and put it home.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Quick, quick, fear nothing; I’ll be at thy elbow.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: It makes us, or it mars us, think on that,

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: And fix most firm thy resolution.

lines.speaker: RODERIGO
lines.text: Be near at hand, I may miscarry in ’t.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Here, at thy hand. Be bold, and take thy stand.
[_Retires to a little distance._]

lines.speaker: RODERIGO
lines.text: I have no great devotion to the deed;

lines.speaker: RODERIGO
lines.text: And yet he hath given me satisfying reasons.

lines.speaker: RODERIGO
lines.text: ’Tis but a man gone. Forth, my sword; he dies.
[_Goes to his stand._]

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: I have rubb’d this young quat almost to the sense,

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: And he grows angry. Now, whether he kill Cassio,

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Or Cassio him, or each do kill the other,

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Every way makes my gain. Live Roderigo,

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: He calls me to a restitution large

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Of gold and jewels that I bobb’d from him,

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: As gifts to Desdemona.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: It must not be. If Cassio do remain,

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: He hath a daily beauty in his life

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: That makes me ugly. And besides, the Moor

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: May unfold me to him; there stand I in much peril.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: No, he must die. But so, I hear him coming.
Enter Cassio.

lines.speaker: RODERIGO
lines.text: I know his gait; ’tis he. Villain, thou diest!
[_Rushes out, and makes a pass at Cassio._]

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: That thrust had been mine enemy indeed,

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: But that my coat is better than thou know’st.

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: I will make proof of thine.
[_Draws, and wounds Roderigo._]

lines.speaker: RODERIGO
lines.text: O, I am slain!
[_Iago rushes from his post, cuts Cassio behind in the leg, and exit._]

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: I am maim’d forever. Help, ho! murder, murder!
[_Falls._]
Enter Othello.

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: The voice of Cassio. Iago keeps his word.

lines.speaker: RODERIGO
lines.text: O, villain that I am!

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: It is even so.

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: O, help, ho! light! a surgeon!

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: ’Tis he. O brave Iago, honest and just,

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: That hast such noble sense of thy friend’s wrong!

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: Thou teachest me,—minion, your dear lies dead,

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: And your unbless’d fate hies. Strumpet, I come!

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: Forth of my heart those charms, thine eyes, are blotted;

lines.speaker: OTHELLO
lines.text: Thy bed, lust-stain’d, shall with lust’s blood be spotted.
[_Exit._]
Enter Lodovico and Gratiano.

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: What, ho! No watch? No passage? murder, murder!

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: ’Tis some mischance; the cry is very direful.

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: O, help!

lines.speaker: LODOVICO
lines.text: Hark!

lines.speaker: RODERIGO
lines.text: O wretched villain!

lines.speaker: LODOVICO
lines.text: Two or three groan. It is a heavy night.

lines.speaker: LODOVICO
lines.text: These may be counterfeits. Let’s think’t unsafe

lines.speaker: LODOVICO
lines.text: To come in to the cry without more help.

lines.speaker: RODERIGO
lines.text: Nobody come? Then shall I bleed to death.
Enter Iago with a light.

lines.speaker: LODOVICO
lines.text: Hark!

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Here’s one comes in his shirt, with light and weapons.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Who’s there? Whose noise is this that cries on murder?

lines.speaker: LODOVICO
lines.text: We do not know.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Did not you hear a cry?

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: Here, here! for heaven’s sake, help me!

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: What’s the matter?

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: This is Othello’s ancient, as I take it.

lines.speaker: LODOVICO
lines.text: The same indeed, a very valiant fellow.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: What are you here that cry so grievously?

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: Iago? O, I am spoil’d, undone by villains!

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: Give me some help.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: O me, lieutenant! What villains have done this?

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: I think that one of them is hereabout,

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: And cannot make away.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: O treacherous villains!
[_To Lodovico and Gratiano._]

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: What are you there?

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Come in and give some help.

lines.speaker: RODERIGO
lines.text: O, help me here!

lines.speaker: CASSIO
lines.text: That’s one of them.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: O murderous slave! O villain!
[_Stabs Roderigo._]

lines.speaker: RODERIGO
lines.text: O damn’d Iago! O inhuman dog!

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Kill men i’ the dark! Where be these bloody thieves?

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: How silent is this town! Ho! murder! murder!

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: What may you be? Are you of good or evil?

lines.speaker: LODOVICO
lines.text: As you shall prove us, praise us.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: Signior Lodovico?

lines.speaker: LODOVICO
lines.text: He, sir.

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: I cry you mercy. Here’s Cassio hurt by villains.

lines.speaker: GRATIANO
lines.text: Cassio!

lines.speaker: IAGO
lines.text: How is’t, brother?

lines.speaker: CASSIO
